question.text:
Consider the given properties of Asymptotic Notations:
I. f(n) = θ(g(n)) and g(n) = θ(h(n))
⇒ f(n) = θ(h(n))
II. f(n) = θ(g(n)) if and only if g(n) = θ(f(n))
III. f(n) = O(g(n)) if and only if g(n) = Ω(f(n))
IV. f(n) = O(g(n)) if and only if g(n) = O(f(n))
Which of the following are valid?

answer.explanation:
Transitivity:
f(n) = θ(g(n)) and g(n) = θ(h(n))
⇒ f(n) = θ(h(n)) valid for Ω and O notations also.
Symmetry:
f(n) = θ(g(n)) if and only if g(n) = θ(f(n))
Transpose symmetry:
f(n) = O(g(n)) if and only if g(n) = Ω(f(n)).
Choice (B)
